title: A $2,200 move-in paid to a poster who did not own the house

steps.label: Listing seen
steps.detail: A renter in the Houston area finds a house for rent on Craigslist.

steps.label: Says he is the landlord
steps.detail: The poster says he is the landlord and gives her a door code, so she can let herself in and see the house.

steps.label: Asked to pay to move in
steps.detail: The poster asks for $1,100 rent and a $1,100 deposit before she moves in.

steps.label: Paid $2,200
steps.detail: She pays $1,100 rent and a $1,100 deposit, part of it borrowed from a friend, and moves in.

steps.label: Found out
steps.detail: Two days later the real owner, a rental company, tells her the poster does not own the house. She is told to leave, and her bank will not refund the money.

findings.text: Taken in this home (3 of 3 photos).
Not confirmed. Owner of record: Invitation Homes, not the poster.
NOT SHOWN. Being inside does not mean they may rent it.
The ad asks you to pay rent or a deposit before move-in, and the owner of record is not the poster.
Invitation Homes, the owner of record, says: "we only accept applications and leasing funds through invitationhomes.com" (invitationhomes.com/preventing-leasing-fraud, read 2026-11-14).

cant_catch: A door code gets the poster and the renter inside, so a photo from inside proves nothing about who may rent the house. SNAPBACK cannot catch a poster when the owner of record is a private person who rents through family, or when the county roll has no owner for the house.
